paragraphs.text: Once a page is printed, its letters become small shapes of ink. We read those shapes as words, while a camera measures their light and dark edges. This study asks whether both readers can use the same honest page.

paragraphs.text: Our first duty is to keep the writing clear. A larger opening letter can mark a new paragraph, but the smaller body still needs room to breathe. Spaces, punctuation, and the rhythm of a sentence belong to the design.
